title: Comparative Performance of Partial Indirect Adhesive Restorations Fabricated Using Three Commercial Lithium Disilicate Ceramics
official: A Randomized Clinical Trial on the Comparative Performance of Partial Indirect Adhesive Restorations Fabricated Using Three Commercial Lithium Disilicate Ceramics
summary: The aim of the study is to compare the clinical behavior of lithium disilicate inlays and onlays with Initial Lisi Block (GC), Cerec Tessera (Dentsply Sirona) and IPS e.max CAD (Ivoclar Vivadent), all fabricated by digital technique (CAD/CAM), at 12, 24 and 36 months after placement. Using this digital technique, the restoration is milled on a machine from the information obtained from your tooth with an intraoral camera. This technique and the materials to be used in your restorations are currently used for the fabrication of the inlays that will later be cemented in the mouth. This implies that they are accepted and regulated by the competent health authorities. This treatment will be performed by Noelia Sanz Herrero, a dentist and student of the Master Degree in Continuing Education in Aesthetic Restorative Dentistry and Endodontics at the Universidad Rey Juan Carlos.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* 1\. Age of patients between 18-70 years. 2. Absence of periodontal disease. 3. Asymptomatic posterior teeth without pulp or periapical pathology with or without root canal treatment.

  4\. Teeth with caries, extensive fractures or previous defective restorations. 5. There must be an antagonist tooth and at least one tooth adjacent to the tooth to be treated.

  6\. Presence of at least 20 teeth in the mouth (natural or rehabilitated with dental implants).

  7\. Possibility of isolating with rubber dam.

Exclusion Criteria:

1. Patients with active periodontal disease at the time of the study will be excluded. 2.
2. Pregnant or breastfeeding women.
3. Patients who present allergy to composite resins and/or adhesive systems.
4. Patients with poor oral hygiene.
5. Polymedicated patients or those chronically prescribed anti-inflammatory drugs.
6. Patients with multiple untreated carious lesions.
